record.paper_title: Unsolved Problems in Visibility Graphs of Points, Segments and Polygons
record.original_question: Does every visibility graph G with minimum degree delta(G) have vertex-connectivity at least (2 delta(G) + 1) / 3?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 6 Every visibility graph G with minimum degree delta(G) has vertex-connectivity at least (2delta(G)+1)/3.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let P be a finite set of points in the plane, no three collinear restrictions need not apply. The visibility graph G of P has vertex set P, with two points u,v ∈ P joined by an edge if and only if the open line segment uv contains no other point of P. Let δ(G) denote the minimum degree of G and let κ(G) denote the vertex-connectivity of G (the minimum number of vertices whose removal disconnects G or leaves a single vertex).

Prove or disprove: For every visibility graph G of a finite point set in the plane,
   κ(G) ≥ (2 δ(G) + 1) / 3.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture remains open in general. Payne, Pór, Valtr, and Wood (Discrete & Computational Geometry, 2012; arXiv:1106.3622) proved κ(G) ≥ δ(G)/2 + 1 for all non-collinear visibility graphs, and proved the conjectured bound κ(G) ≥ (2δ(G)+1)/3 in the special case where at most four points are collinear. They also showed the bound, if true, is tight. No complete resolution was found in subsequent searches.

status_evidence.title: On the connectivity of visibility graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Vertex-connectivity is at least half the minimum degree, and in the case that ℓ=4 this bound is improved to two thirds of the minimum degree.
status_evidence.claim: Partial result: κ≥δ/2+1 in general; κ≥(2δ+1)/3 proven only when at most 4 points are collinear.

status_evidence.title: On the Connectivity of Visibility Graphs - Discrete & Computational Geometry
status_evidence.snippet: Bounds on edge- and vertex-connectivity of visibility graphs of point sets in the plane.
status_evidence.claim: Published partial progress towards the (2δ+1)/3 vertex-connectivity conjecture for visibility graphs.
